svg.title: Automated Spark diagnostics: pulling logs and metrics through Fabric's REST API instead of clicking through the Spark UI
svg.desc: A flow diagram contrasting manual Spark UI troubleshooting across five overlapping surfaces with an automated pipeline that resolves application identifiers, calls Fabric's Spark monitoring REST API (an OSS Spark History Server mirror plus Fabric-only advice/resourceUsage/logs endpoints), pulls the raw event log, parses it into skew/spill/critical-path findings, maps findings to named remedies, and produces a severity-ranked report — with branch lanes for Livy bootstrap failures and the continuously-pushed diagnostic emitter, plus warning callouts for common REST fetch failures and emitter misconfiguration.
svg.text: Automated Spark Diagnostics — REST API and Event-Log Pipeline vs Manual Spark UI
Resolve ids ➔ call the Spark monitoring REST API ➔ pull & parse the event log ➔ rank findings ➔ map to a named remedy
Fabric Codex Original

g.text: Automated pipeline (fact)
Branch lane (Livy / emitter)
Pattern (remediation)
Warning (documented failure)
Manual baseline (contrast)

g.aria-label: Manual path: five overlapping UI surfaces
g.title: Manual path: five overlapping UI surfaces — Without automation, troubleshooting is spread across five overlapping Spark UI surfaces that look like one.
g.text: MANUAL BASELINE · CONTRAST
Without automation: five overlapping Spark UI surfaces, navigated one at a time
In-cell live progress · in-cell Spark Advisor panel · Recent runs / Monitoring hub · tabbed Application detail (Jobs/Resources/Logs/Data/Diagnostics) · full Spark History Server
A human must know which surface holds the answer and reassemble a diagnosis from scratch every time.
FACT

svg.text: Automation replaces UI tab-hopping with identifier resolution

g.title: Resolve identifiers from a description — An automated diagnostic tool resolves workspace and item identifiers from a plain-English description before calling any API.
g.text: STEP 1 · RESOLVE IDENTIFIERS
"The nightly ETL notebook failed again" → workspaceId, itemId, livyId, applicationId, attemptId
Fabric Spark Operations Skill (preview): resolves ids from a plain-English description
Scenarios: health review · root-cause analysis · pipeline-failure tracing · Livy session triage
FACT

svg.text: Resolved ids drive the REST endpoint path
A session that never started routes here

g.aria-label: Livy log: the only view into bootstrap failures
g.title: Livy log: the only view into bootstrap failures — A whole class of Fabric Spark failures happens before any Spark job exists and is visible only in the Livy log, never the Spark UI's job/stage/task tabs.
g.text: BRANCH · LIVY LOG
Bootstrap failures exist before any job does
Capacity 430s, library conflicts,
unpublished Environments, timeouts —
visible ONLY in the Livy log, never
in job/stage/task REST data.
Three separate log streams:
• Livy — submission, lifecycle, queuing
• Prelaunch — warmup, pool allocation
• Driver — stdout/stderr, stack traces
Skill also detects stuck/zombie Livy
sessions burning capacity idly.
WARNING

g.title: Spark monitoring REST API — Fabric exposes Spark application internals as a REST API that mirrors the OSS Spark History Server contract exactly.
g.text: STEP 2 · REST API SURFACE
Mirrors the OSS Spark History Server contract
Same endpoints, params, JSON shapes for
jobs, stages, tasks, executors, storage, streaming
/v1/workspaces/{wsId}/notebooks|sparkJobDefinitions|
lakehouses/{itemId}/livySessions/{livyId}/applications/
{appId}/{attemptId}/{endpoint}
Auth: in-notebook Fabric REST client, or
Entra app / service-principal token externally
Wrong item-kind segment (notebooks vs
sparkJobDefinitions vs lakehouses) 404s.
FACT

svg.text: Same surface, Fabric-only layer

g.title: Fabric-only endpoints: advice, resourceUsage, logs — Beyond the OSS contract, Fabric adds an advisor-findings endpoint, an executor resource-usage endpoint, and a raw driver-log endpoint.
g.text: STEP 3 · FABRIC-ONLY ENDPOINTS
No open-source equivalent
advice
Spark Advisor Info/Warning/Error findings
as structured JSON, filterable by stage/job/executor
resourceUsage
Executor CPU/memory over time — the Resources
tab's chart as thresholdable numbers
logs?type=driver
Raw driver stdout/stderr text, fetchable
without opening the Fabric portal
FACT

svg.text: The same REST surface also serves the raw event log

g.aria-label: Pull the raw event log for post-hoc analysis
g.title: Pull the raw event log for post-hoc analysis — Pulling the raw event log via REST is the direct route for post-hoc analysis of one specific past run, surfacing detail the portal UI does not expose.
g.text: STEP 4 · PULL THE RAW EVENT LOG
Post-hoc analysis of one specific past run, on demand — no advance setup needed
Same raw SparkListener JSON-lines stream the Spark UI renders from. Surfaces detail the
portal UI never exposes: exact per-stage skew ratios, spill attribution, a true critical-path
ranking of stages, and the application's real effective configuration as ground truth.
FACT

svg.text: On-demand pull vs
the continuous push
Malformed requests fail five documented ways

g.title: Five common event-log fetch failures — Fetching a Spark event log via REST fails for five common, well-defined reasons, most often a missing attemptId segment.
g.text: WARNING · FIVE FETCH FAILURES
In order of frequency
1. Missing /{attemptId}/ path segment (usually 1, or 2 after retry) → 400/404
2. Wrong item-kind segment — SJD app under /notebooks/ 404s
3. Pasting the portal Monitoring-hub URL directly — not a valid endpoint
4. Copy artifacts: stray quotes, trailing slash, fragment, query string
5. Querying an application that hasn't finished — event logs finalize only on completion
The toolkit's URL normalizer accepts 6 real-world pasted shapes and
repairs all five causes before calling the endpoint.
WARNING

g.title: Alternative: the continuously-pushed diagnostic emitter — The diagnostic emitter streams logs and metrics continuously to Log Analytics, Storage, or Event Hubs as an alternative to pulling the event log on demand.
g.text: BRANCH · CONTINUOUS PUSH
The push alternative to pulling on demand
Streams driver/executor logs + metrics continuously to
Log Analytics, Azure Storage, or Event Hubs. Configured as
Environment Spark properties — session-start scope only.
Same raw event stream, but pushed continuously instead of pulled after the fact.
FACT

svg.text: Configuring the push has its own failure modes

g.title: Four documented emitter gotchas — Configuring the Log Analytics diagnostic emitter has four specific, documented gotchas that silently produce an emitter collecting nothing.
g.text: WARNING · FOUR GOTCHAS
Silently collects nothing, no error shown
1. skipStarterPools must = true, or a starter
pool never engages the emitter (most common)
2. Category-name list differs by destination —
copying one example into the other collects nothing
3. Secret = Log Analytics workspace primary key,
not an Entra token or connection string
4. Job submitters need Key Vault read access to the
secret, or the emitter fails to initialize per session
WARNING

svg.text: A successful pull is parsed in one pass
Emitter branch also feeds the ranked report below
Bootstrap causes are ranked alongside job-layer causes

g.aria-label: Parse the event log into ranked findings
g.title: Parse the event log into ranked findings — A single pass over the parsed event log ranks stages by their real wall-clock contribution and reports skew ratio and spill volume for each.
g.text: STEP 5 · PARSE INTO RANKED FINDINGS
Stage-ranking by real wall-clock share (the "critical path")
One pass over the parsed event log reports each stage's % share of total duration,
alongside its skew ratio and spill volume — not task count or stage id order.
Effective config (AQE, shuffle partitions, NEE/ANSI flags) is recovered directly
from the event log's own environment-update event — ground truth, not assumption.
Worked example — a real executed run with a deliberately skewed join
70% of a 1.2M-row table's rows on one key vs a 500-row table. Detector measured
a genuine 3.8x skew ratio (max 1733ms vs median 457ms, 16 tasks) — exceeding its
own 3.0x threshold → critical finding. Recovered shuffle-partition count (16) matched.
FACT

svg.text: One companion metric is estimated, not measured

g.aria-label: Shuffle-size estimate is a proxy, not a measurement
g.title: Shuffle-size estimate is a proxy, not a measurement — A companion shuffle-partition-count heuristic is explicitly labeled a starting-point proxy, not a measurement, and must be validated against real Shuffle Write metrics.
g.text: WARNING · ESTIMATE, NOT MEASUREMENT
A companion shuffle-partition heuristic is a proxy, not a measurement
max(input bytes / 128MB, 2× executor vCores) — a groupBy that aggregates away most rows shuffles far
less than input size suggests; a row-exploding join shuffles more. Validate against the real Shuffle Write metric.
WARNING

svg.text: Each ranked finding maps to a named fix

g.title: Physical-plan-to-remediation mapping — Five recurring Fabric Spark slowness signatures each map to a specific plan/log fingerprint and a specific remedy.
g.text: STEP 6 · FINGERPRINT → REMEDY
Five recurring slowness signatures, each with a named fix
Zero data skipping
FileScan reads = table's total file count → set dataSkippingStatsColumns + cluster on filter col
NEE fallback
Alternating VeloxColumnarToRow/RowToVeloxColumnar in driver stderr → replace the causing UDF
Severe skew
Large median-vs-max task-duration gap in Stages tab → AQE skew join or explicit key salting
SortMergeJoin spill
Large Spill (Memory)/(Disk) metrics → lower AQE advisory partition size or force broadcast join
Small-file task explosion
Tens of thousands of sub-150ms tasks in Jobs tab → OPTIMIZE to consolidate V-Ordered files
PATTERN
Applying a generic tweak instead of the fingerprint-matched remedy can miss the actual cause.

svg.text: Emitter path also feeds the same ranked report
Bootstrap causes ranked alongside job-layer causes
Advisor findings and resource usage feed the report

g.title: Severity-ranked diagnostic report — The automated pipeline's output is a severity-ranked diagnostic report, not raw logs a human still has to interpret.
g.text: RESULT · SEVERITY-RANKED REPORT
A ranked report to act on — not raw logs to interpret
Read-only: identifies stuck/zombie Livy sessions, ranks findings by severity, attaches the fix.
FACT

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Fabric Spark REST/monitoring internals, the Fabric Spark Operations Skill blog, and first-party Spark toolkit notebooks.
